title: SDK proctoring labs and eval scenarios (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures an early draft of "proctored" SDK labs and evaluation scenarios intended for: (1) robust onboarding for new integrators, (2) internal certification for developer advocates and SEs, and (3) reproducible quality checks for SDK releases. The focus is on short, supervised labs (15–90 minutes) that exercise common failure modes and guardrail patterns which matter for production usage on Redwood (hosted + dedicated + private).

Context / why now:
- Were seeing repeated FAQ patterns from pilots about error handling, auth, and local-mode emulation.
- New Dedicated/private customers want deterministic test flows for acceptance.
- Developer advocates need a compact way to validate SDK behavior across model variants and network conditions.

Scope (what this doc contains):
- Lab types and proctoring levels (self-serve -> guided -> proctored exam)
- Concrete evaluation scenarios (quickstarts + failure injection + performance smoke checks)
- Scoring rubric and pass/fail criteria for certification
- Minimal infra/automation requirements and checklists for proctors
- A 15-minute quickstart lab script for first-contact sessions

Non-goals:
- Full course curriculum (this is a lab-level draft, not a 2-day bootcamp).
- Deep pedagogy; assume attendees know basic REST/HTTP and have a dev laptop.

Audience:
- external integrators (pilot customers)
- internal SEs / dev advocates / onboarding team

Lab taxonomy (proposed):
1) Quickstart Smoke (self-serve, 10–15m)
   - Primary goal: make first SDK call, receive streaming tokens, basic error handling.
   - Environment: hosted sandbox token, single small example model, zero infra.

2) Guided Failure Probe (guided, 30–45m)
   - Primary goal: simulate network flakiness, token expiry, and fallback to smaller model.
   - Environment: sandbox + local proxy to simulate latency/HTTP 5xx.

3) Proctored Certification (proctored, 60–90m)
   - Primary goal: validate an engineers ability to integrate SDK, instrument telemetry, and implement graceful degradations.
   - Environment: reserved seat on Dedicated mirror environment OR scripted private deployment.

Example evaluation scenarios (concrete steps):
A. First-call quickstart (Quickstart Smoke) — 15m script
   1) Setup: clone minimal sample app (git clone https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/tree/labs/minimal-quickstart)
   2) Auth: set REDWOOD_API_KEY in shell, confirm using `redwood whoami` (sample helper).
   3) Run: `npm run lab:start` or `python quickstart.py` — produce a streaming chat output.
   4) Verification: verify streaming tokens arrive and final message contains the string "redwood-quickstart-success" that the harness injected.
   5) Report: paste the console log to the lab form.

B. Failure injection + fallback (Guided Failure Probe) — 45m
   1) Pre-reqs: local proxy script (provided) and sandbox key.
   2) Step: cause proxies to return 502 for model "base-1" and observe SDK retry/fallback to "base-1-compact" per routing policy.
   3) Expectation: SDK should log a retry (x2), emit a telemetry event `sdk.fallback.model`, and surface a user-level error only if fallback fails.
   4) Evaluation: Proctor checks logs + telemetry; runs a scripted test in CI to confirm no unhandled exceptions.

C. Offline-mode + latency simulation (Proctored Certification) — 90m
   1) Deploy a tiny private runner with on-prem config (instructions in infra repo).
   2) Run a long prompt sequence, force KV-cache eviction, and measure token latency before/after caching.
   3) Candidate must: implement prefix caching hook, patch SDK config to enable batching=auto and quantization profile=fast, and show improved per-token latency in the provided metric dashboard.
   4) Score: latency improvement >=20% and no incorrect retries.

Scoring rubric (suggested):
- Quickstart Smoke: pass if end-to-end demo completes and logs uploaded (auto-graded).
- Guided Probe: points across checkpoints (auth, retry behavior, telemetry). Must reach 70% to pass.
- Proctored Certification: multi-part checklist: correctness (40%), observability (30%), stability under injection (30%). Threshold: 80%.

Proctor checklist (minimal):
- Confirm candidate identity and seat allocation (Dedicated sandbox mapping)
- Provision sandbox keys and temporary dataset
- Ensure lab harness (logging + telemetry) is reachable
- Start recording terminal session logs + optional screen share
- Triage infra issues: have a quick-fix script for common failures (proxy restart, token refresh)

Instrumentation + automation needs (infra backlog):
- Lightweight harness repo: `sdk-labs/harness` (auto-creates ephemeral sandbox keys, captures logs, generates verification tokens).
- Dockerized local proxy to inject latency and errors (configurable policies).
- Small dashboard: lab instance status, telemetry spike view, and candidate report uploader.
- CI smoke tests per SDK release wired to a subset of labs (smoke + fallback tests).

15-minute Quickstart lab (step-by-step script for reps):
- Target audience: 1:1 customer quickstarts and demo pods.
- Pre-req (5m): ensure GitHub repo cloned, node/python env installed, REDWOOD_API_KEY set.
- Exercise (8m): run sample app, observe streaming, change prompt input and re-run.
- Wrap (2m): copy paste logs into the intake form + one-line reflection: "What surprised you?"

Sample verification checklist for Quickstart (auto-graded):
- tool ran without fatal error: true/false
- streaming event count > 0: true/false
- verification token present in last message: true/false

Accessibility / accommodations:
- Provide extended time option for candidates with needs (45/120 min variants).
- Provide recorded guided walk-through for self-serve labs.

Content for handouts (short bullets to include in slides):
- 3 minute intro: what the SDK guarantees (auth, streaming, fallback, telemetry)
- 5 minute demo: first-call, streaming tokens, graceful fallback example
- 7 minute hands-on: run quickstart and change prompt

Open questions / decisions to make:
- Which environments can we safely use for proctoring without incurring heavy infra cost? (Dedicated mirror vs ephemeral private cluster)
- How "strict" should proctored criteria be for external partners vs internal cert?
- Should we have a paid certification for partners? (business question, route to partnerships team)
- What minimum telemetry retention is needed to support post-lab audits? (privacy/compliance input required)

Next actions (short):
1) Priya: draft the harness README and minimal CLI to generate ephemeral keys (JIRA-DE-987).
2) Diego: build the local proxy container and add latency/error presets (PR target: sdk-labs/proxy#5).
3) Evan: prototype the auto-grader for the Quickstart (upload + verification token).
4) Aisha: schedule a 60-minute sync with SRE/infra to scope Dedicated mirror cost and runtime templates.

Notes to self (rough):
- Keep the proctor flow low-friction: try to avoid manual infra steps that need SRE on the call.
- Lean on telemetry events (sdk.*) rather than asking for raw logs when possible.
- Consider lightweight badges (digital) for passing internal certs so SEs have a visible incentive.

References / links to copy/paste into handouts:
- Quickstart repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/tree/labs/minimal-quickstart
- Harness ticket: JIRA-DE-987
- Example telemetry events: sdk.request.start, sdk.request.retry, sdk.fallback.model, sdk.cache.hit

End of draft.

Unresolved: attach estimated effort in story points once infra sync complete.
